> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7a606a9a3409e121e524f51542f5375815a22a35` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b93340d7e827e271812fdd7c02b513a8c98cd87e` — the merge of head `f692a171c06e40668fbfa126d13d7ec0920b673e` into base `7a606a9a3409e121e524f51542f5375815a22a35`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b93340d7e827e271812fdd7c02b513a8c98cd87e && git checkout b93340d7e827e271812fdd7c02b513a8c98cd87e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7a606a9a3409e121e524f51542f5375815a22a35 f692a171c06e40668fbfa126d13d7ec0920b673e && git checkout -B drift-repro 7a606a9a3409e121e524f51542f5375815a22a35 && git merge --no-ff f692a171c06e40668fbfa126d13d7ec0920b673e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7a606a9a3409e121e524f51542f5375815a22a35
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7a606a9a3409e121e524f51542f5375815a22a35` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f692a171c06e40668fbfa126d13d7ec0920b673e`
Local-runs: none

Isolated reviewer, read at 2026-10-01T09:11Z. Inputs and nothing else: card #21063 (body and all four comments: the queue-jump relay `5924780893`, triage's ruling `5925000390`, the claim `5925129243`, the dev report `5928018705`), PR #21134 (title, body, six-file list, and the net diff from the merge base `9c8b65aa` to the head, which GitHub's diff and a local three-dot diff agree on byte for byte), the head's check-runs, and, as the card names them, PR #21051 and its contract review `5924418816`. The head is a merge of `main`; the eleven commits `main` has gained since the merge base touch none of the six paths. Files at the head were read with git show only: nothing built, run, or re-run. ⚠️ Security card: everything below is stated by class and position only.

### Gate verdicts, read off the head's check-runs

Read last, as the brief asks, and only after the head's CI had finished: an earlier reading found eleven runs still in progress (the six Test Core shards and their rollup, Lint & Repo Gates, Temporal Conformance, and two Type Check leaves); the final reading found none. 35 check-runs on the head, all completed, every one bound to this head: 32 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke: path-filtered or opt-in, none a required context), 0 failed, 0 in progress. The required contexts are all `success`: Lint & Repo Gates (which carries `check:generated` and `check:api-surface`), TypeScript Type Check with its four leaves, Test Core with its six shards, the Dogfood Regression Gate with its three shards, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG and MySQL), and the Governed Surface Queue Guard. Also `success`: Check Changeset (the job carrying the ADR-0087 registration gate and the no-major guard), the three claim guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, and Check Documentation Links. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, with the verdict on it.

1. **One derivation, one input moved — right.** The whole runtime change is one line in `resolveCallerPosture`: the zero-set stand-in now carries the posture's per-field capability contract instead of an empty map. Every reader already folds that input through `foldFieldRequiredPermissions`, the ADR-0066 D3 helper, which marks a gated field neither readable nor editable for a caller who does not hold every named capability; a caller with no set holds none (the evaluator's capability set over no sets is empty), so each gated field reads as denied. The stand-in is read at exactly four sites at the head, and I walked each: the engine middleware's `secMeta` (feeding step 2.5, the echo refusal 2.5a, the aggregate-input guard 2.5b, the predicate guard 2.9 and the step-4 result masker), `resolveProjectionFieldMask` (feeding the three published projections and the metadata-plane variant), the ADR-0056 public-form grant branch's echo masker (from PR #21101), and the new `canWriteObject` arm. No second derivation of the fold exists anywhere in the diff. Masking for this class is byte-identical: `computePartialMaskRules` tests whether the caller holds every capability on a rule-bearing field, and that test cannot pass with an empty held set whether the stand-in carries the contract or not, so every rule still applies to this class exactly as since PR #21051.

2. **Read answer for the class: served stored, becomes not served — right, and the ruling's own direction.** Step 4 was never gated on a resolved set; it was inert for this class only because the stand-in carried no field contract. With the contract carried, the masker deletes a gated field that carries no masking rule, and serves masked a field that carries both a gate and a rule (`maskResults` serves any field in the rule map masked even where the fold denies it, and the read projection keeps such a field as a served column). The precedent's pin on the head still asserts the full read set for a fixture carrying both a gate and a rule in this class, so "served masked, as before" is pinned, with the suite's conclusion on the head as the verdict. The explain engine is untouched by the diff: it reads the real posture and folds it over the resolved sets, which for this class is the empty set, so it reported the field hidden before and still does; the new pin asserts the door and explain agree per class case. `getReadableFields` answers the full set minus the gated-and-unmasked fields; `getMetadataReadableFields` answers the same when the fallback set resolves nothing and the caller carries a principal, and still the full set for a principal-less context (the "no FLS posture here" tier), which is what the corrected docblock says.

3. **Query accept set for the class: a filter, sort key, group key or aggregate input naming a gated field, admitted becomes refused — right.** Steps 2.9 and 2.5b read `computeQueryGuardFieldPerms`, which applies the same fold; `getQueryableFields` reads the same map, and the new pin proves the projection equal to both guards field for field across the four positions.

4. **The write side (the seat's question 1): inside the ruling, inside the claim's surface, and right.**
   - Inside the ruling. Triage's ruling adopts the field's own describe as the protocol for that field, quoting it: "mask on read, deny on write". That is the published `requiredPermissions` describe on the field schema and ADR-0066 D3's AND-gate, which is one gate over read and write. The ruling then says the plugin folds "the gate" into the stand-in as it folds masking, and forbids a second derivation. The fold is one helper that marks a gated field both unreadable and uneditable, so carrying it moves `getWritableFields` for this class mechanically (the write projection excludes every field the fold marks non-editable). The published write contract says the answer is "the exact complement of the fields that gate refuses when a payload names them"; once the projection narrows, that sentence holds only if step 2.5 refuses the same fields for this class. The only way to narrow the read answer without touching write would be a read-only variant of the fold, which is the second derivation the ruling forbids. So the write edits are what the ruling's own constraints force, not an extension of it.
   - Inside the claim's surface. The claim names the plugin's source tree and the spec contract file as the surface; its ⛔ lines are object admission and row scope for this class, the REST and analytics doors, and the public-form doors. The field-level write gate and the write projection are none of those. The third docblock (`getWritableFields`) is in the claimed file, follows from the same fold, and the dev declared it as a deviation.
   - Right, step 2.5 ungated. For this class the evaluator's field map over no sets is empty, the fold adds only the gated fields as denied, and `detectForbiddenWrites` flags only fields present in that map, so the gate refuses exactly the capability-gated fields and nothing else: "deny on write", as declared. For every caller with a resolved set the new helper `computeForbiddenFieldWrites` is the old inline code step for step (evaluator map, fold, delegator intersection, an empty map answers an empty list, then the detector), so that class is unchanged. A principal-less context is handed through before any gate and never reaches 2.5. The delegator intersection is null for this class in the middleware (delegator resolution sits behind a resolved set), and the helper is handed null, so the two readers of the helper agree.
   - Right, the `canWriteObject` arm. With a payload and a principal, arm 4 now asks the same helper over the same stand-in with the same null delegator, so the preview answers as the write path does. On an unreadable posture it fails closed, which is where the middleware has refused this class since PR #21051 (the stand-in carries the resolved flag), so this is the preview catching up to enforcement, not a new object-level decision; the arm is reached only when a payload is supplied, and the preview probe always supplies one. The PR body declares this.
   - One wording residual, not a defect: the plugin-security changeset's sentence that whether this caller may read or write the object at all is unchanged is true of enforcement (the middleware's object-level gates are untouched), while the preview probe's answer for a payload-carrying ask on an unreadable posture moves from admit to deny for this class. The PR body states that corner; the changeset covers it by the sentence that the write preview answers such a payload as the write path does.

5. **No other class moves (the seat's question 2) — verified, right.** A caller with at least one resolved set reads the real posture; the stand-in is never consulted for it. Step 2.5's inner computation for that class is the old code; `canWriteObject`'s arm 9 for that class is the old code through the same helper. A principal-less context short-circuits in the middleware before any gate, takes the projection's early full-set answer, and is excluded from the new arm by the same predicate; the new pin asserts the full set and admission for it. A system context bypasses everywhere. The one door that inherits the narrowing without being touched is the public-form grant's echo read-back, which resolves the grant context's sets and reads the stand-in for a context resolving none: that submitter is this class at another door, not a different class (PR #21101 defined a grant context as never the principal-less hand-off), and the dev named it in the report and the PR body. The grant's bypass of step 2.5 on the write itself is pre-existing and applies to every caller through that grant; it is the public-form doors' surface (#21062), outside this card. Nothing widens anywhere: the fold only adds denied entries, the unmask test cannot pass for an empty held set, and arm 4 only gained earlier denials.

6. **Object admission for this class is unchanged — verified, right.** The stand-in's object-level capability contract is still the frozen empty contract, and its private and tenancy flags are still false. At the head the middleware's capability AND-gate and its CRUD gate both still sit behind a resolved-set guard, and `canWriteObject`'s arms 6 to 8 still sit on the resolved-set branch. The one corner the dev reported (the preview probe asked with no payload still admits this class on an unreadable posture while the middleware refuses) is this class's object admission, correctly left to the services split of #21061 direction 2, and unreachable from the preview door, which always supplies a payload.

7. **Pins, red then green.** The new file pins the three ways the class arises, each asserting the zero-set premise first, then per case: door versus explain, the two read projections, the query projection versus both guards in four positions, and the write gate versus the write projection versus `canWriteObject` field for field; controls for a capability holder and a set lacking the capability; and the principal-less boundary. The existing write-projection pin's one zero-set case now expects the narrowed answer and checks the middleware agrees. The dev's red run (12 class cases failing on the pins commit), the green run, and the three ablations (the stand-in line, the 2.5 gate, the arm) are the dev's readings; the suite's conclusion on the head is CI's. Fixtures are synthetic.

8. **Public surface.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` moves in docblocks only; no method, parameter, type or export changes, so the published type surface is unchanged and the published prose (which ships in the declaration file) narrows three answers for one class. The stale sentence in `getMetadataReadableFields` (the middleware "skips its whole field gate") that PR #21051's review escalated to this lane is corrected to the grant gates. No hand-written doc states a zero-set field answer; the one page naming the projections is the system-context page, about a system context, which is unchanged. Nothing is falsified.

9. **Disclosure discipline of the PR's own public text — kept.** The title, the body, both changesets and the new pin state the caller class, the field class, the readers and the positions; the only names are synthetic fixtures; no door, object or field from a private reading is named, and nothing reads as a request recipe.

10. **Consumers.** The approvals snapshot (read projection intersected with the query one), the analytics field gate (both projections), metadata-core (`getMetadataReadableFields`) and objectql (`canWriteObject` through the write-preview probe) all take the narrowed answer for this class by construction; the dev ran their suites at the pre-merge commit, and the head's Test Core shards are the verdict.

### ② Semver level

- Two changesets, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-security`, each at `minor` with a bang in the title, a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and one ADR-0087 marker. Both packages are published, so each needs one; `skip-changeset` would be wrong. The PR body's line 2 and the claim carry the identical declaration.
- Level: right. The repo's rule is that `yes` takes at least `minor` and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, and the launch-window guard forbids `major`, so `minor` with a bang is the one legal spelling of a breaking narrowing.
- Clause-② arm: `yes (narrowing)` is right. The path arm hits (a non-test file under the spec contracts) and the declaration arm hits; a published contract answer narrows for one caller class, and nothing widens for any class (① items 5 and 6). PR #21051's `no (narrowing)` was right for a diff that touched no contract file; this diff does.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` on both: right. Nothing an author can write is removed, renamed or re-meant; no stored shape, spec key, schema or export moves; neither body carries a FROM to TO prescription (each "What to do" paragraph is prose: fold the field contract as for any set lacking the capability; grant the capability or drop the requirement). The Check Changeset run, which carries the registration gate and the no-major guard, is the gate verdict.
- The BREAKING text: the plugin-security body states the class as the exact complement of the principal-less predicate (a position, a named set or a user id), the subclass that stays served masked, the four refused query positions, the write refusal, the moved projections and the remedy. The spec body states the three narrowed answers for implementers and consumers and names the reference implementation. One wording residual is in ① item 4; it does not misstate enforcement.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared; none found.
- Dev deviations, each answered: (1) the write-side surface (step 2.5 ungated, the `canWriteObject` arm, the one helper): judged in ① item 4 as inside the ruling and the surface, and load-bearing. (2) The `getWritableFields` docblock sentence: in the claimed file, forced by the same fold, right. (3) Consumer suites measured before the merge of `main`: the merge brought PR #21101's edit to the grant region of the same file; the net diff at the head shows this PR's hunks untouched by it, and the head's CI is the verdict. (4) A closure build cut by the dev's own outer timeout and re-run without it: a process note, no effect on the diff. (5) No real-boot reading of the doors: the doors read the same step 4 the pins drive with the real plugin, PR #21051's dogfood pin exercises this class on real doors, and the Dogfood Regression Gate's conclusion stands as the gate verdict. All five accepted.
- Out-of-scope findings, both rightly left unfiled by the dev and carried to the seat: (a) the preview probe asked with no payload admits this class on an unreadable posture while the middleware refuses; object admission, carrier the services split of #21061 direction 2, no reach from the preview door. (b) The public-form read-back now drops a gated field for a submitter who resolves no set; it follows from the one derivation and is not pinned at that door. Escalated as a note to the services seat that owns the public-form doors: one case at that door would close the pin gap.
- The escalation PR #21051's review sent to this lane (the stale metadata-plane docblock) is closed by this diff.
- The adjacency the cli seat raised (stand alone, fold into, or order after #21061 direction 2): triage graded the card standing alone, and because this diff leaves object admission for the class untouched it composes with that split in either order.
- The PR is a draft with no landing label; flipping it is the seat's act under the landing rules, not a review matter.
